source: Oldenburg et al. 1998 Figure 3 solid experimental curves; previously audited 31 points per sample
opticalData: Equal-weight Olmon single-crystal / McPeak complex-permittivity average

electronScattering.length: 4V/S, both inner and outer metal-shell interfaces

distribution: Independent lognormal number distributions of core radius and shell thickness; one identical core population for every sample in each family
normalization: One positive amplitude per spectrum in the paper’s arbitrary image-height units. No baseline, wavelength shift, refractive-index fit or adjustable A. Residuals normalized by each experimental spectrum maximum.

bounds.sharedCore: fixed to the labelled population fits

native.quadrature: Exactly the lesson fine setting: 25 nodes, or 41 if a number CV exceeds 25%; nodes below weight 1e-16 omitted

defaultReason: Both families retain good whole-spectrum and held-out agreement with modern Au, A=1 and one shared core distribution per family. These optical fits do not uniquely establish the particle distributions.

rising.interpretation: Candidate complete thin shell. The spectrum has no observed maximum within the figure and the shell geometry is not uniquely identified.
rising.sharedCore: The core distributions remain fixed to the three labelled completed-shell spectra. The rising spectrum supplies no extra freedom in the core sizes.
rising.backgroundAssumption: A nonnegative constant vertical plotting offset is fitted for the rising trace. It registers the spectrum in the figure and is not a physical background in lesson 05 or the Lightbox. The missing maximum still prevents a unique structural inference.

defaultPopulationRowSelection: Use the shared-core population fits for labelled spectra and the background group for the rising trace. Its constant is a vertical plotting offset.
